abstract: Energy harvesting from vibrating systems represents an alternative for reducing pollution, fossil fuel consumption and other environmental externalities associated to road transportation. While a variety of technological schemes has been proposed for harvesting vibrational energy from vehicles, the resultant devices have not been competitive with other energy recovering systems such as regenerative braking (EGB). In this paper, a simulator for the operation of an energy harvester accessory is presented, in which the harvester is installed around the damper of an existing suspension system as the vehicle travels on a rough pavement. The relative motion of the chassis and suspension is used to generate the electrical energy through two magnets and a coil. The transition matrix approach is considered to solve the equations of motion of different vehicles, while the visualization software is based upon MATLAB. Results suggest that power outputs can reach up to 100 W when a two-axle vehicle travels on a poor condition road. The potential implementation of the system is further discussed.

articleTitle: PD trajectory tracking control without velocity for rigid robots with PMSM
abstract: This paper proposes a solution for the problem of global trajectory tracking with a PD controller plus feedforward of rigid robots equipped with PMSM (Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor) when the electric dynamics of these actuators are taken into account. Besides, here is replaced numerical differentiation by the high pass filter in the PD controller. Thus, we shown that proposed controller produces global convergence to the desired link positions using Lyapunov. Moreover, the result is extended to n degrees-of-freedom.

articleTitle: Face segmentation using mathematical morphology on single faces
abstract: The face segmentation is an important step for face recognition because it is not only locates the face but also get a correct segmentation for a fuller region possible. In this paper an application of the viscous opening along the skin color for segmentation and obtaining the limit of facial contour is presented. The proposal consists of two stages: the first one use the classification of pixels based on skin color given an input image to find the region of interest; in the second stage, the viscous opening is used to generate two markers of the resulting image from the previous stage, with the objective of maintaining only the facial area, avoiding the neck area.

articleTitle: DFT study of PVDF as polymer composite precursor
abstract: The superior physicochemical and mechanical properties of polymer composites (PCs) can be attributed to the interfacial interaction between additives, such as ceramics, clays or metals; and the polymer matrix. In PCs, both additives and the polymeric matrix interact at a level that modifies the electromechanical properties. Firstly, the article offers an insight in literature reported modeling techniques related to simulation of the electromechanical and polar response of PCs. In the subsequent step, the results obtained from quantum chemical calculation performed for poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF), as starting PCs study, are reported. The actual density functional theory (DFT) methodology has been focused to evaluate the electronic properties of this polymer in order to predict its average macroscopic response to an external impulse, e. g., an electrical potential.

articleTitle: Biocompatibility of liposomes derived from microbial cells: an assesment towards Nanomedicine applications
abstract: The emergence of Nanotechnology in Medicine has resulted in the development of a wide set of nanocarriers. One of the most popular approaches in drug delivery is the use of liposomes, which are self-assembled lipid bilayers. Mammalian-derived liposomes are known to be highly biocompatible. However, the toxicity of liposomes prepared with microbial lipids is still to be clarified. Strains from the genus Mycobacterium are able to induce a high immune response in humans, which is known to involve the responses towards the amphipathic lipids they synthesize, and various reports have proposed the use of mycobacterial liposomes as adjuvants and vaccine boosts. In this work, M. fortuitum and M. tuberculosis lipids were used to produce mycobacterial-derived liposomes, and their physical and chemical characterization, as well as biocompatibility vis-a-vis human cells are addressed.

articleTitle: Volumetric behavior of a mixture of Portland cement with sodium bentonite: Experimental design of an alternative commercial expansive cement
abstract: The shrinkage phenomenon present in the elements made with Portland cement generates problems of cracking if this is restricted to bending stress, this causes aesthetic problems and eventually structural problems. Expansive cements exist in the market that reduce cracking but its economic value makes it uneconomical to use. This document discusses the volumetric behavior after setting and during early-age hardening in a mixture with Portland cement incorporating different amounts of bentonite during a period of 48 hours, during which the volume changes are greater.

articleTitle: Evaluation of supported Au-TiO2 catalyst over different substrates for methyl red dye removal
abstract: In this paper several methods for titanium dioxide (TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) synthesis are presented, the methods used were microwave assisted sol-gel, anodizing and plasma deposition, and these structures were also doped with Au. The obtained morphologies were characterized by Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and elemental analysis EDS, also its catalytic effectiveness was measured by the degradation of the methyl red dye in water by photocatalysis and photo-electrocatalysis test. As well as the mineralization ratio was recorded by the total organic carbon removal. The kinetic study was carried out in order to determine the behavior of the reaction in each color degradation.

articleTitle: Photocatalytic electrolyzer prototype based in a material using TiO2-Pt
abstract: TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-Pt photocatalysts have been synthesized by a sol-gel proccess microwave-assisted and characterized by means of several techniques (Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), powder X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Raman spectroscopic techniques) and used in the hydrogen generation under UV irradiation at room temperature. Crystals of anatase phase (size about 24 nm) was obtained, as confirmed by XRD. The morphology is regular and agglomerates are formed as the dopant (SEM) is added. TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-Pt material was used to make electrodes (working and counter), for his use in a photocatalytic electrolizar for the production of hydrogen, the first UV tests were successful, the material can produce hydrogen. The material will be tested in different concentrations (Pt) in the electrochemical cell to obtain a relationship between the cost and the production of hydrogen.

articleTitle: Urban freight transport planning policies in the metropolitan zone of Tijuana
abstract: Planning in cities deals with the most appropriated ways to implement improvements and development strategies, so that the population can be the most beneficiated. International agencies are urging to implement new policies and strategies in order to tackle the transportation emissions causing climate change. It is then considered important to analyze how much urban freight transport (UFT) has been included in the planning policies in Mexican cities. As a case study, we analyze the metropolitan area of Tijuana City, who has experienced a dramatic trend of growth and development in recent years. The method consists in an extensive review of the development plans, programs, legislation and/or regulation documents available. An effort of compilation, systematization and a synthesis of measures addressed to UFT was performed. The results shows that there is a lack of UFT related-policies, however evidences show too that the government has an interest to generate proposals to join government, society and businessman to better understand this issue.

articleTitle: Potassium acrylate copolymer and agave fiber as improvers of stone substrates for greenhouse production
abstract: Success in greenhouse production is due, in part, to the use of a well-characterized substrate and a suitable fertigation schedule, among others. The behavior of several mixtures of stone substrate (tezontle, pumice) with improvers (potassium acrylate copolymer and agave fiber) was evaluated in this research. The physical properties of the resultant mixtures, such as water- and air-retention, drainage and apparent density. Were measured and then, the energetic state of the mixture (Field Capacity (FC)) was calculated in laboratory. Afterwards, the mixtures were exposed to irrigation in greenhouse conditions; the FC and drainage were measured. T-3 (pumice with 8g of potassium acrylate copolymers) and T-6 (pumice agave fiber) were distinguished by having a favorable moisture retention, T-1 (pumice) was selected as control. These treatments were carried in a greenhouse cucumber crop cycle.

articleTitle: Use of fly larvae (Musca domestica) in feed for Macrobrachium sp.
abstract: In the present study, the potential of fly larvae meal as a protein source for incorporation in a diet used in culture animals of the genus Macrobrachium is evaluated. Two experimental feeds were formulated based on meal larvae, with differences in protein content (25 and 35%); they were provided to individuals of the genus and compared opposite with two commercial foods with the same percentage of protein, for a period of 90 days to determine the following response factors: survival rate, growth rate, feed conversion and protein efficiency. The experimental results show that feeds have acceptable yields in the first 60 days of work, however, at concluding the work, the highest yields were presented in the commercial feed with 35 % of protein.

articleTitle: Fuzzy c-means clustering for steady state events classification of electrical signals
abstract: Improving the efficiency of the electricity usage is an important concern these days relaying on monitoring techniques mainly divided into two categories: the intrusive monitoring that is focused on measure the power consumption of each electrical load individually and the non-intrusive monitoring which measure the power consumption from a centralized point and determine which electrical loads are presented. Electrical signatures are the main components of a non-intrusive monitoring system; these signatures are presented on the transient and steady state events on the signal. In order to classify these events according to its signatures, it is necessary to detect when and where these events occur. This work presents a method to detect and classify steady state events using the fuzzy c-means clustering algorithm; the proposed method is based on a frequency domain analysis, more specifically the analysis of the fundamental frequency and the first odd harmonic in order to improve the computational cost of the event classification algorithm.

articleTitle: Thermal feasibility of tilapia production under greenhouse conditions in a semi-desert region of Mexico
abstract: Nile tilapia do not achieve the desired productivity in the semi-desert regions of Mexico, because of their temperature variations. Temperature needs to be regulated to obtain commercial weights in 6 months, as stated by governmental agencies. With the use of greenhouses it is not possible to maintain all year round the optimum water for tilapia production, thus the temperature effect needs to be considered. A comparison was performed between two different semi-arid environmental temperatures. Fingerlings were stocked (60 days) by triplicate inside a greenhouse. Water, greenhouse and environmental temperatures were measured. Fish were weighed at the end. The weekly average values were compared graphically. External temperatures were of 20.5 ± 6.7 (ET=20.5) and 16.9 ± 8.4 °C (ET=17) respectively. ET=20.5 °C showed a more stable water (26.8 ± 1.3 °C) and greenhouse temperatures (24.4 ± 4.4 °C) while ET=17 °C had a greater variation of water (22 ± 3.3 °C) and greenhouse (18.7 ± 5.5 °C) temperatures. Tilapia under ET=20.5 °C achieved a better weight of 22.23 ± 1.85 g whit a tendency for bigger weights while Tilapia under ET=17 °C achieved a more uneven weight of 16.21 ± 3.30 with a tendency for smaller fish. The temperature and growth variation will have to be considered when planning a tilapia production project to obtain the desired weights. Tilapia under greenhouse in semi-arid regions of Mexico, without any other technology, will only be feasible, according to the plans proposed by the government, during the warmer period of the year.

articleTitle: Recycled aluminum modified with MWCNT for structural spatial truss applications
abstract: Due to the environmental damage caused for the steel manufacture, an alternate material that is less harmful to the ambience is proposed. It consists of recycling aluminum from beverage cans by melting and remelting in a furnace creating a composite reinforced with carbon nanotubes to magnify the mechanical properties of strength and being able to use it structurally where the strength-self-weight ratio is important as truss.

articleTitle: Photoelectrocatalytic degradation of methyl red dye using Au doped TiO2 photocatalyst
abstract: Au-TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> photocatalyst have been synthetized by a microwave assisted sol-gel method and characterized by means of X-ray diffraction techniques (XRD) and UV-vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy. Photoelectrocatalytic degradation of methyl red dye have been carried out and a 95% degradation was achieved.

articleTitle: An assessment of the effectiveness of speed controlling devices in descending slope roads
abstract: In Mexico, different traffic calming devices are being used. For highways, the federal government has issued some criteria for the installation and geometrical distribution of small buttons that cross the roads, particularly in descending slopes, willing to reduce, by 10%, the traffic speed. However, there is the perception that such devices do not effectively reduce the traffic speed. In this paper, a field study is described of two different principles to assess the effectiveness of such devices to calm the traffic, installed in two highway locations. While one methodology was based upon a speed gun, mounted in a following car, the second one was based upon the analysis of videos of a traffic before and after the speed controller devices. Both analysis confirmed a poor performance of such devices to reduce the traffic speed, as only 15% of the scanned vehicles reduced their speed, as most of the vehicles showed an increased speed at the end of the speed control road segments.
